title: Weighted polyglot request dispatcher for multi-region latency and capacity SLOs
creator: Daniel Park
description: Problem: Our current steering policies lean heavily on latency hedging and static geo-pinning. Under regional capacity pressure (autoscale lag or noisy neighbors) this results in cascading cross-region hedges, SLO violations, and opaque backpressure behavior for customers. Goal: Implement a single, explainable dispatcher that combines latency signals, geo-affinity, and capacity headroom into a stable weighted routing decision. The dispatcher should import circuit-breaker state and tokenized load-shedding budgets, expose debugging traces, and allow gradual rollout. It must reduce p95/p99 latency SLO violations and keep cross-region traffic within configurable budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Dispatcher computes a deterministic weight per candidate region using: latency score, geo-affinity score, capacity headroom, and optional cost multiplier.

When a region's capacity drops below configured headroom threshold, dispatcher reduces weight smoothly (hysteresis) and stops hedging traffic into overloaded regions for at least the configured hold window.
Integration with circuit-breaker: trips are honored and cause immediate weight zero for the trip window. Untrip uses exponential backoff probes.
Soft load-shedding: requests are shed proportionally via token budgets (per-tenant and global) rather than blunt rejects; shed decisions emit metrics and traces for every affected request.
Observability: dashboard with per-region weight distribution, SLO burn rate, rejected/shed counts, and example traces. Traces must correlate to original request id.
Simulation: end-to-end simulator shows >=30% fewer SLO violations under synthetic regional degradation scenarios compared to existing latency-only hedging policy (baseline).
Rollout can be toggled per-account and supports canary (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) with automatic rollback on SLO regressions.
tasks: Design scoring function and document math (latency z-score normalization, headroom-to-weight mapping, geo-affinity decay).
Implement dispatcher plugin in request-router with pluggable scoring components and safe default weights.
Add circuit-breaker hook: subscribe to region state store and incorporate trip windows into weight calculator.
Tokenized shedding implementation: per-tenant fast-path and global backstop with fair-sharing algorithm.
End-to-end integration tests and chaos scenarios (region CPU spike, disk saturation, network traffic delay).
Build simulator harness that replays real production traces and synthetic degradations to compare policies.
Create Console dashboard tiles and tracing hooks; add alerting for unexpected shed rates and sudden weight shifts.
Run staged rollout and capture SLOs for canary cohorts; implement rollback triggers (burn rate > 2x baseline or error rate spike).
Write runbook entries and postmortem checklist for routing incidents referencing this dispatcher.

2025-02-22 - Marina Lopez (SRE): Ran initial simulator with 10k synthetic requests over 24h traces. Early result: latency-only hedging had 18% more p99 violations during a region CPU spike. Polyglot weighting reduced p99 by 12% and reduced cross-region traffic thrashing. Added simulation notes.

2025-02-27 - Oliver Chen (Platform): Circuit-breaker integration proposed: use existing cb-store events with 'tripped' and 'probe' states; dispatcher must honor tripped at once. We should avoid heavy polling; suggest push via local cache subscriber.

decisions: Use a weighted-sum scoring model that is explainable and debuggable (decision made 2025-02-19).
Hysteresis windows will be applied to headroom changes to avoid oscillation; default hold window = 90s (decision 2025-02-20).
Circuit-breaker tripped state forces weight=0; probe windows use conservative fixed traffic fraction (0.1) until stable for 3 consecutive probes (decision 2025-02-25).
Prefer proportional shedding over blunt rejection; tenants get proportional allotments based on recent usage and priority tiers (decision 2025-02-26).
rollout_plan: Feature flag off in prod by default.
Canary 1% traffic for non-sensitive tenants for 24h. Monitor p95/p99 latency and error budget burn.
Expand to 10% if no regressions in 48h. Run chaos test (regional CPU spike) against canary group.
Expand to 50% with aggressive alerting and auto-rollback if burn rate > 2x baseline.
Full rollout to all tenants after 7 days of stable metrics and resolved feedback.
notes: Simulator setup: replays production region affinity and injects degradations. Baseline: existing latency-only hedging. Polyglot policy config: latency_weight=0.5, headroom_weight=0.35, geo_affinity=0.15.
Preliminary simulation (2025-02-22): reduced SLO violations by ~43% in a mixed degradation test (one region saturated for 10min bursts every hour).
Operational hooks: exporter emits per-request 'dispatch_reason' tag: LATENCY|HEADROOM|GEO|CIRCUIT_BREAKER|SHED. Useful for downstream billing and compliance audits.
Open questions: how to incorporate cost multiplier per region for customers on Dedicated? Proposal: allow per-tenant cost_weight override behind an enterprise flag.
